The Framingham approach

More room to explore.

Build your visit around what appeals to you: warmth, water, stillness, or a dedicated therapy appointment. There is no prescribed sequence. Our team can help you choose a starting point, and you can move at your own pace.

Available in Framingham

Explore the experiences.

Both locations

Infrared sauna

Gentle infrared warmth for a slower moment in your day.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. A warming, restful experience; some small studies report improvements in pain and well-being.

What to know. Evidence is limited, and findings from traditional saunas do not automatically apply to infrared sessions.

Before you try. Check with your clinician before use if pregnant or if you have heart or blood-pressure conditions. Avoid heat when unwell or dehydrated; stop if dizzy.

Research review ↗ · Heat & pregnancy ↗

Both locations

Cold plunge

A cool-water immersion experience, on its own or alongside warmth.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. May reduce muscle soreness after strenuous exercise compared with rest alone.

What to know. Short-term relief does not mean faster muscle growth or proven long-term health benefits.

Before you try. Cold water changes breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure rapidly. Speak with your clinician first if you have heart, circulation, or breathing conditions. Do not plunge alone or hold your breath.

Recovery evidence ↗ · Cold-water safety ↗

Both locations

Normatec compression

Rhythmic air compression around your legs while you recline.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. May offer modest relief from post-exercise soreness and the feeling of tired legs.

What to know. Studies show small or inconsistent effects on strength and performance recovery.

Before you try. Do not use with known or suspected blood clots, acute infection, or acute heart failure. Ask the team and your clinician about wounds, fractures, or circulation concerns before use.

Recovery review ↗ · Manufacturer safety ↗

Framingham

BrainTap meditation

Guided audio and a light-and-sound headset for a focused pause.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. Meditation practices may help with stress and sleep; choose a guided program or music experience.

What to know. Research on meditation in general does not establish the same benefits for the BrainTap headset.

Before you try. Flashing lights can trigger seizures or blackouts. Consult your physician before using the headset if you have a seizure history, photosensitivity, brain injury, or another serious condition.

Meditation evidence ↗ · Headset safety ↗

Framingham

Salt chamber

A quiet salt-lined setting for time away from the everyday.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. A dedicated space to sit quietly, unwind, and enjoy the atmosphere.

What to know. Evidence for treating respiratory or skin conditions is limited. Salt-room visits do not replace prescribed treatment.

Before you try. If you have asthma or another lung condition, check with your clinician before exposure to airborne salt. Leave if you notice coughing, wheezing, or irritation.

Evidence review ↗

Framingham

Eucalyptus steam room

Moist warmth with eucalyptus, as part of your Framingham visit.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. Enjoy the sensory contrast of humid heat and a quiet break between other experiences.

What to know. Comfort is personal. Evidence does not establish steam-room visits as a treatment for respiratory illness or detoxification.

Before you try. Avoid overheating and leave if lightheaded or short of breath. Check with your clinician about pregnancy, heart conditions, or heat-sensitive conditions; tell us about eucalyptus sensitivity.

Heat & pregnancy ↗

Framingham

Warm-water hydrotherapy

Settle into the warm water of our Framingham hot tub.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. Warmth and buoyancy offer a different way to rest and feel supported in the water.

What to know. This is a recreational soak, not supervised aquatic rehabilitation or a treatment for injury.

Before you try. Talk to your clinician before use during pregnancy. Avoid alcohol and overheating, and follow posted water-safety guidance. Stay out if you have diarrhea.

Hot-tub safety ↗

Framingham

BioCharger

A seated light-and-frequency experience in a dedicated space.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. Choose a program and take a quiet, seated pause during your visit.

What to know. Independent clinical evidence for this specific device remains limited; benefits for energy, immunity, or cellular repair are not established.

Before you try. Electronic implants and photosensitivity need special screening. If you have a pacemaker, defibrillator, insulin pump, or seizure history, speak with your clinician and the team before entering the session area.

Manufacturer precautions ↗

Framingham · Premium

PEMF therapy

A separate appointment using pulsed electromagnetic field equipment.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. Some clinical studies suggest short-term relief of pain and stiffness in knee osteoarthritis.

What to know. Results depend on the condition, device, and protocol; they are not a promise for our spa sessions or evidence of whole-body healing.

Before you try. Consult your clinician first, especially with an implanted electronic device or during pregnancy. Confirm suitability for the specific equipment with the team before booking.

Research review ↗ · Clinical overview & safety ↗

Framingham · Premium

Flowpresso

Full-body compression, gentle warmth, and deep pressure in a dedicated appointment.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. An enveloping sensory experience designed for rest and winding down.

What to know. Early device-specific research explores sleep and stress, but strong independent evidence is still limited. We do not promise detoxification or medical outcomes.

Before you try. Ask the team to review the device screening with you. Get clinical advice before use if pregnant or if you have blood-clot, heart, circulation, or heat-sensitivity concerns.

Device research ↗

Benefits vary by person, equipment, and session. These notes are a starting point, not a complete contraindication list or medical advice. Ask your healthcare professional about suitability and tell our team about relevant conditions before your visit. Medical disclaimer (PDF) ↗
